Subject: Post-call: security + retention pathways and next steps

Hi Tom / LifeSpring IT team —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the immediate asks we discussed so your security and compliance team can triage: 

- SOC 2: Redwood is currently in progress on Type II; we shared a high-level timeline on the call and can provide interim artifacts (control matrix, auditor point of contact) for your review.
- Data types and retention needs: you indicated two buckets — PHI logs (from product telemetry) and app metadata (non-PHI).
- Backups & snapshots: you asked whether backups can outlive configured retention windows and how deletion is handled (soft delete vs full purge).
- Legal hold / eDiscovery: you want a documented process for placing holds and confirming preserved backups.

Immediate asks / next steps: 
1) Please confirm the retention window you need for PHI logs (options you mentioned: 90 days or 180 days) and whether you require immutable snapshots for any period.
2) Complete the attached vendor security questionnaire (VSA_Questionnaire.xlsx) — we can pre-fill sections if you want.
3) Let us know whether you need a formal retention exception policy and an SLA for purge confirmation (typical audits ask for proof-of-deletion).

Attachments: VSA_Questionnaire.xlsx (attachment), SOC2_status_summary.pdf (attachment).

I propose a 30-minute technical follow-up next week (I have Wed/Thu mornings PT). If you share the retention requirement above we can scope pricing implications and backup windows.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Vanessa —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifying questions so our security team can move faster: 

1) When you say "deletion" — does Redwood remove data from live stores only, or are backup snapshots and incremental backups also removed at the same time? We need to understand whether a retained backup could contain data after an apparent deletion window.
2) What is the default backup retention and can we set separate retention for backups containing PHI?
3) Do you support legal holds that suspend deletion automatically? If yes, how is that evidenced to auditors?
4) We need encryption details for backups at rest (algorithms/key management) and whether keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed.

Also, can you provide a sample retention SLA or playbook that outlines RPO/RTO for restores and confirmation of purge? If you can send those items ahead of a follow-up call that would be ideal.

Best,
Tom Brennan
Head of IT Security, LifeSpring Health
it-security@lifespring.health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: security + retention pathways and next steps

Hi Tom —

Appreciate the clear list of questions. Below are concise answers and attached artifacts for your auditors. Happy to walk through any item on a short call.

1) Deletion vs backups/snapshots\- Redwood's deletion API removes data from the active store immediately. Backups and snapshots are retained according to the configured backup retention window and are considered part of the customer's retention policy. When a record is "deleted" from the application it will no longer be returned by queries; however, if a backup snapshot exists that was taken before the deletion it will persist until its retention expires or a legal hold is applied. We can configure backup snapshot retention separately for PHI.

2) Default backup retention and per-bucket policies\- Default backup retention: 90 days. We support per-dataset retention policies and can set a longer retention (e.g., 180 days) for datasets marked as PHI. We can also offer immutable snapshot options for contractual needs (additional cost).

3) Legal hold / eDiscovery\- We support a legal hold API that marks datasets/snapshots as preserved; preserves suspend automatic purge and are tracked with an auditable event log. Upon hold release we run a purge job; we provide certificate-style evidence for purge completion (timestamped job IDs and manifest). We'll share the standard evidence package used for audit purposes.

4) Encryption and key management\- Backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256. By default Redwood manages keys, but we offer customer-managed keys (KMS) integration for enterprise/private deployments (bring-your-own-key via supported cloud KMS or HSM for on-prem). We'll include the KMS integration guide in the attachments.

Attached: SOC2_summary_v2.pdf (interim controls and timeline), Retention_SLA_Playbook.docx (policy template + purge evidence examples), Backup_RTO_RPO_Table.csv (standard RTO/RPO options).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the PHI retention window (90 vs 180 days) so we can surface pricing for immutable snapshots if needed.
- Complete the VSA (we can pre-fill technical sections) and return.
- Schedule a 30-minute technical call this week to review proof-of-deletion flow and KMS options.

If useful, here's our expected SOC 2 Type II completion: November 2026; interim evidence available on request at the link below.

Link: https://redwood.app/oss/soc2-evidence-request-form

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
